questions.question: Which annotation turns on @PreAuthorize checks in a Spring Boot app?
questions.explanation: @EnableMethodSecurity switches on the checks. Without it the method annotations are ignored.

questions.question: What is the main difference between @PreAuthorize and @PostAuthorize?
options: @PreAuthorize checks before the method runs, @PostAuthorize checks the returned value after it runs
@PreAuthorize is for roles only and @PostAuthorize is for users only
questions.explanation: The Pre version decides whether the method may start. The Post version runs the method and then checks its result.

questions.question: A method has @PreAuthorize("#patientId == authentication.name"). User p101 calls bills("p102"). What happens?
options: The method returns the bills of p102
An AccessDeniedException is thrown and the web caller gets 403
The method returns an empty list
questions.explanation: The argument p102 does not equal the username p101, so the rule is false and access is denied.

questions.question: A list method returns three appointments and has @PostFilter("filterObject.doctor() == authentication.name"). Two belong to drrao. What does drrao receive?
questions.explanation: @PostFilter removes every element for which the expression is false, so only drrao's two remain.

questions.question: A service method has @PreAuthorize("hasRole('ADMIN')"). Another method in the same class calls it directly with this.deleteAll(). Why does a normal user get through?
options: The call goes around the security proxy, so the rule is never checked
hasRole always returns true inside a class
The user must have been an admin
questions.explanation: Method security works through a proxy. A call from inside the same object skips the proxy, so no check happens.
